item.title: Rail Link project on the move
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: The next stage of the Sunshine Coast’s major passenger rail project has taken another step forward, with a consortium led […]
item.content:encoded:
The next stage of the Sunshine Coast’s major passenger rail project has taken another step forward, with a consortium led by SunLinQ awarded the design and pre-construction contract for the line between Caloundra and Birtinya.

The contract marks a significant milestone for Stage 2 of The Wave, which will extend the proposed rail network north from Caloundra, bringing new stations, improved transport connections and a tunnel beneath Little Mountain.

SunLinQ brings together BMD Constructions, CPB Contractors, GS Engineering and Construction Australia and UGL Engineering.

The State Government said the contract award would accelerate planning and detailed design for the seven-kilometre dual-track rail extension, which will include new stations at Aroona and Birtinya.

Major construction is expected to start in early 2027, subject to Australian Government environmental approval.

Site investigations are already underway to inform the planning and development of the detailed design, with community consultation on the Stage 2 station precincts scheduled for early next year.

The broader vision for The Wave is to connect the Sunshine Coast from Beerwah through Caloundra and Birtinya, with a future extension towards the Sunshine Coast Airport.

The project is being positioned as a major response to the region’s rapid population growth and increasing pressure on the road network, providing an alternative for commuters travelling to work, education, health services and other destinations.

Minister for Transport and Main Roads Brent Mickelberg said the contract award was a major milestone in delivering a modern transport network for the Sunshine Coast.

“We’re moving ahead with delivering a transport network that meets the need of the Sunshine Coast, now and into the future,” Mr Mickelberg said.

Minister for Housing and Public Works Sam O’Connor said the project would connect people to jobs, education, healthcare and other opportunities.

“The Wave will connect people to jobs, education, healthcare, entertainment and opportunity while supporting the biggest investment in Sunshine Coast infrastructure in the region’s history,” he said.

Member for Caloundra Kendall Hatcher said the milestone was another step towards improving transport connections for growing communities.

The project is expected to support about 3300 jobs across Stages 1 and 2, while creating opportunities for local businesses and suppliers and supporting future housing and economic growth.

The State Government says the rail project will complement other Sunshine Coast transport infrastructure, including the Mooloolah River Interchange and Caloundra Congestion Busting Plan.

When operational, The Wave will also benefit from Queensland’s permanent 50-cent public transport fares.

Stage 1, extending the rail line from Beerwah to Caloundra, is jointly funded by the Queensland and Australian governments.

However, the Queensland Government says the Federal Government has not committed funding to Stage 2, which is the subject of the latest contract announcement.

item.title: Noosa’s penthouse record
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: EXCLUSIVE Noosa’s prestige property market has delivered another extraordinary result, with a three-bedroom beachfront penthouse selling for $21.5 million – […]
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE

Noosa’s prestige property market has delivered another extraordinary result, with a three-bedroom beachfront penthouse selling for $21.5 million – a new record – at auction last weekend.

The La Mer Apartment 13 penthouse, at 37 Hastings Street, Noosa Heads, attracted eight bidders, with the spirited contest culminating in a sale that sets a new record for an apartment and an auction sale anywhere on the Sunshine Coast.

The result eclipses the previous apartment record of $16.1 million, achieved in 2021 when the same agency sold Apartment 5 at nearby Hastings Park.

The auction, held on site, attracted a packed crowd, with the hammer fall greeted by what selling agent Tom Offermann described as the loudest round of applause he could remember at an auction.

The property was a particularly rare offering, being one of only 10 beachfront penthouse apartments with a roof terrace along Noosa’s coveted beachfront strip.

It was also the first time in six years that a three-bedroom apartment directly on Noosa Main Beach had come onto the market.

The seller had purchased the apartment 12 years ago for $5.3 million, meaning the latest transaction represents an increase of $16.2 million over that period.

Tom Offermann said the auction attracted eight bidders, all of whom were long-term clients with a history of owning, or currently owning, investment property in Noosa.

“With eight bidders fighting for the ultimate prize, the hammer fell at $21.5 million, accompanied by the loudest round of applause I can remember at an auction,” he said.

“Three bidders were still in the fray after it hit $20 million, so that’s the social proof of value.”

The apartment’s rooftop terrace, absolute beachfront position and sweeping northerly views across Laguna Bay, Noosa Main Beach and the Noosa National Park were among its standout features.

The two-level property includes three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a series of outdoor entertaining areas, a residents’ swimming pool and direct access to the beach.

Mr Offermann said the sale reflected the scarcity of prestige property along Noosa’s beachfront, with values continuing to climb as exceptional properties changed hands.

The sale rate worked out at about $90,000 per square metre, slightly above the approximately $88,000 per square metre achieved in several previous transactions, including a nearby two-bedroom Tingirana apartment which sold for $10.2 million.

The new apartment record comes just two months after Offermann’s agency sold a Noosa Parade waterfront home for $40 million, setting the benchmark for a residential house sale in the area.

The penthouse auction also capped a strong week for the agency, which recorded $70 million in unconditional transactions, including two Noosa Sound waterfront homes at 19 Key Court and 24 Noosa Parade.

Mr Offermann said prestige property remained in tight supply, but buyers continued to demonstrate significant purchasing power when the right property became available.

“There are a lot of people in the market with significant buying power, and although most took a back seat after the Treasurer’s shock May Budget announcements, by their actions they are telling us that life is short and they are getting on with their lives,” he said.

“When they find a property that will enhance their lives, they are not going to hold back.”

The $21.5 million result further reinforces Noosa’s position as one of Australia’s most tightly held prestige residential markets, where limited beachfront opportunities continue to attract buyers prepared to pay a premium for an irreplaceable location.

item.title: Cooroy facility hits market
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: A substantial industrial facility in Cooroy is being offered for lease, providing a significant opportunity for businesses seeking space in […]
item.content:encoded:
A substantial industrial facility in Cooroy is being offered for lease, providing a significant opportunity for businesses seeking space in one of the Noosa region’s tightly held industrial precincts.

The property at 4 Jarrah Street comprises a 5800sqm site with approximately 2254sqm of building accommodation, including offices, enclosed warehousing and a large covered open-sided storage area.

Colliers Sunshine Coast agents Jesse Howitt and Nick Dowling are marketing the property, which is vacant and ready for occupation.

The facility is being offered at an asking rent of $275,000 a year, plus outgoings and GST, through a tender process closing at 4pm on Tuesday, December 1.

The property is zoned Medium Impact Industry and is suitable for a range of uses, including manufacturing, warehousing, storage, distribution and associated industrial operations.

Its location within the Cooroy Industrial Park is a major attraction, with the property approximately 1.6km from the Bruce Highway interchange, 1.5km from Cooroy railway station and about 20 minutes from Noosa.

The building includes 1312sqm of covered open-sided warehouse and storage accommodation, alongside enclosed warehouse space and office facilities.

Other features include extensive concrete hardstand, generous onsite parking and vehicle manoeuvring areas, two-way access from Jarrah Street and prominent signage exposure.

The facility also has air-conditioning to the workshop, painting bay, offices and lunchroom, an air compression system and a 46kW solar power installation.

The property offers businesses access to the wider Sunshine Coast, Noosa and Wide Bay regions, with the Bruce Highway providing a direct transport connection.

Cooroy’s industrial precinct has become an important employment and business hub for the Noosa hinterland, accommodating warehouse, distribution, processing and trade-based operators.

“The availability of a facility of this size provides an opportunity for an established business looking to expand or relocate, as well as operators seeking a strategic base close to the Bruce Highway,” Mr Howitt said.

Colliers estimates annual property outgoings, excluding GST, at approximately $17,132.56, covering council rates, Unitywater, insurance and property management.

Mr Howitt said the property presented an opportunity to secure a long-term leasehold over a functional industrial facility in a sought-after location.

The tender process closes at 4pm on December 1, 2026, subject to Noosa Council procurement process conditions.

For further information, contact Jesse Howitt on 0468 495 640 or Nick Dowling on 0419 726 705 at Colliers.

item.title: Artist’s coastal impressions
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: Winning the hearts of hundreds of art lovers has proved the perfect springboard for Marcus Beach artist Kathy Gallagher, who […]
item.content:encoded:
Winning the hearts of hundreds of art lovers has proved the perfect springboard for Marcus Beach artist Kathy Gallagher, who returns to Pomona Railway Station Gallery this weekend for her first solo exhibition.

Kathy was named the People’s Choice winner at the gallery’s inaugural Local Emerging Artist Prize in September, with her impressionist-style pastel painting The Blue Umbrella capturing the imagination of visitors to the exhibition featuring 40 finalists.

Now she is returning with Noosa Impressions, an exhibition celebrating the beauty of everyday moments along the Sunshine Coast, from changing light across the water to people enjoying simple pleasures by the sea.

The exhibition opened on Saturday, 21 November, and runs until Wednesday, 16 December.

A retired doctor, Kathy says art has always been part of her life, although it took retirement and a change of lifestyle to pursue her passion more seriously.

“Art was always a hobby, but I never studied it as I followed the maths/science line,” she says.

That changed about seven years ago when she discovered soft pastels, sparking a passion that has continued to grow.

Her move to Marcus Beach three years ago provided further inspiration, with the coastal environment offering an endless supply of subjects.

Living near the beach has sharpened her eye for the seemingly ordinary – the changing moods of the sea, shifting light on the water and people sharing quiet moments together.

Noosa Impressions invites visitors to pause and appreciate those fleeting experiences, including daily beach walks with her husband and two dogs.

Through her mastery of light and colour, Kathy uses soft pastels to create works ranging from energetic and vibrant scenes to peaceful coastal moments.

Some paintings capture the vitality of beach life, while others encourage viewers to enjoy the tranquillity of the ocean, whether alone or in the company of friends.

Pomona Railway Station Gallery president Ron Collins said Kathy’s return was a fitting reflection of the gallery’s 25-year history of providing a launching pad for emerging local artists.

“At its heart is its unwavering commitment to supporting local and emerging artists,” Ron said.

“So many artists have appreciated the warmth, friendliness and encouragement of gallery volunteers, finding the support and courage they needed to take the next vital steps in their careers.”

The not-for-profit gallery is managed and operated by volunteers and is celebrating its 25th anniversary this year.

For Kathy, the solo exhibition represents another important step in an artistic journey that began with a childhood interest and found renewed purpose through retirement and life on the coast.

item.title: Pumping with action
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: A highly anticipated new pump track is now open on the Sunshine Coast, giving riders of all ages an exciting […]
item.content:encoded:
A highly anticipated new pump track is now open on the Sunshine Coast, giving riders of all ages an exciting new place to have fun and connect with friends and family.

The new facility at Lions and Norrie Job Park in Coolum, jointly funded by Sunshine Coast Council and the Queensland Government, is the centrepiece of the latest upgrades to the popular park on David Low Way.

Designed with input from the local community, the pump track offers a dynamic riding experience that allows users to generate momentum through body movement rather than pedalling.

The track welcomes bikes and skateboards and caters to a range of ages and skill levels.

The project was identified as a community priority in the park’s landscape plan and has been delivered alongside a range of park improvements, including an additional barbecue shelter, better path connections, upgraded fitness stations, a shade sail and landscaped spaces that link the pump track to the rest of the park.

Sunshine Coast Council Division 9 Councillor Maria Suarez said she was stoked to see the long-awaited facility open and ready for the community to enjoy.

“This is a fantastic outcome for Coolum and our wider community,” Cr Suarez said.

“The pump track has been designed by the local community including students from the schools, and it will be incredibly rewarding to see local riders finally enjoying the facility they helped shape.

“Whether you’re learning the basics, improving your skills or simply having fun with family and friends, there’s something here for everyone.

“We heard loud and clear that the community wanted a track that delivered excitement, challenge and connection, and that’s exactly what has been created.

“I can’t wait to see the track come alive with activity and becoming another great place for our community to be active, healthy and outdoors.”

Member for Ninderry Dan Purdie said the new pump track was a strong win for local families, delivering a much-loved community facility that gives riders of all ages more opportunities to get outdoors, stay active and have fun.

“The Queensland Government has provided $550,000 in funding for the project, in addition to $250,000 for improvements to local parks, to create spaces where communities can get outdoors and enjoy everything that Coolum has to offer.”

Community feedback helped inform the design from concept to completion, with riders sharing ideas on features such as taller jumps and pumps, crossover opportunities, jumpable lines, higher drop-ins and tabletop jumps.

The new pump track complements the park’s existing recreational facilities, including the basketball half court, a destination north of the river for young people, families and visitors to enjoy.

Pump tracks continue to prove popular across the Sunshine Coast, joining successful facilities at Sugar Bag Road Town Reserve in Caloundra West and Forestwood Drive Park in Buderim.

The pump track is jointly funded by Sunshine Coast Council and the Queensland Government.

Sunshine Coast Council invested $350,000 to help deliver the new pump track, leveraging an additional $550,000 from the Queensland Government to bring this community-prioritised project to life.

The project builds on the $1.6 million Stage 1 transformation of Lions and Norrie Job Park, which delivered new shelters, barbecues, pathways, fitness equipment and landscaping.

item.title: Choose your own adventure
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: What if you could influence the direction of a theatre performance? What can car repairs teach us about masculinity and […]
item.content:encoded:
What if you could influence the direction of a theatre performance? What can car repairs teach us about masculinity and mental health? And what happens when women’s stories, knowledge and lived experience take centre stage?

These are just some of the ideas behind the projects receiving support through the latest Regional Arts Development Fund (RADF) round, which is helping local artists develop new work, build skills and connect with audiences.

Council and the Queensland Government are investing more than $113,000 combined through RADF to support local artists, creative practitioners and organisations across the region.

Sunshine Coast Mayor Rosanna Natoli said investing in arts and culture was an investment in the community.

“The arts help people connect, spark new ideas and create shared experiences that stay with us long after the event is over,” Mayor Natoli said.

“RADF supports local creatives to take the next step in their artistic journey, while ensuring our community can continue to enjoy diverse and high-quality cultural experiences.

“These projects are another reminder of the talent, passion and creativity that exists across the Sunshine Coast.”

D.I.V.E. Theatre Collective received $15,000 for Choice, an immersive physical theatre production exploring free will, identity and human decision-making.

Developed by a multicultural ensemble, Choice will place audiences at the centre of the action through a unique theatrical experience that explores the choices that shape who we are and how we connect with others.

Artistic Director Cesar Genaro said the funding would help transform the project from an idea into a significant creative opportunity for local artists.

“For independent artists, funding is a powerful vote of confidence in our voices, our stories and our community,” Mr Genaro said.

“Thanks to the RADF grant, Choice isn’t just an idea on paper. It’s nearly 700 hours of paid creative work for seven passionate regional artists.

“We want audiences to step into our space not just as observers, but as active participants sharing a real human connection through immersive theatre.”

Benjamin Burns received $15,000 to further develop Petrol and Repairs, a spoken word theatre work exploring masculinity, mental health and recovery.

Using the familiar world of engines, maintenance and repair as a powerful metaphor for personal healing, the project aims to create a festival-ready production that encourages audiences to reflect on wellbeing, resilience and connection.

Wendy McPhee received $12,613 for Reimagining Jean, a contemporary performance work exploring feminine knowledge, visibility and resilience.

The project will bring together older women and creative collaborators to develop a work that celebrates shared wisdom and perspectives that are often overlooked.

Mentorship funding was also awarded to five Sunshine Coast creatives, supporting professional development in arts leadership, animation, installation, sculpture, experimental sound and interdisciplinary performance.

Strong Community Portfolio Councillor David Law said mentorship was an important investment in the future of the Sunshine Coast’s arts community.

“Having the chance to learn from experienced practitioners is invaluable for creatives at any stage of their journey,” Cr Law said.

“These mentorships connect local creatives with industry leaders, helping them build skills, confidence and professional networks that can benefit their careers for years to come.

“Supporting that growth not only benefits individual artists, it strengthens the Sunshine Coast’s creative community as a whole.”

Discover the full list of RADF recipients on Council’s website.

item.title: Recognition given with Biosphere awards
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: A Year 11 geography class, a team of turtle trackers, and young change makers were among the winners honoured at […]
item.content:encoded:
A Year 11 geography class, a team of turtle trackers, and young change makers were among the winners honoured at the 2026 Noosa Biosphere Awards held at The J in Noosa on Thursday 12 November.

Presented by the Noosa Biosphere Reserve Foundation (NBRF), the awards recognise the people, businesses and organisations protecting Noosa’s environment and strengthening its community.

Seven categories were awarded, with winners chosen from 34 finalists who were announced at Green Drinks in October.

The 2026 Noosa Biosphere Award winners are:

Emerging Custodian Award: Juniper Roo Houston (Highly Commended – Hunter Williams)

Environmental Steward Award: Meghan Halverson

School or Class Biosphere Custodian Award: Noosa Adventist College (Year 11 Geography) for Ecological Hazard: Shark Nets

Social Impact Award: University of the Sunshine Coast for the GroW Cooroy Gardening and Wellbeing Program

Sustainable Business Award (joint winners): Mayan Farm and RACV Noosa Resort

Thriving Nature Award: Teewah Landowners Association Inc. for the Teewah Turtle Trackers Monitoring & Conservation Initiative

Smart Biosphere Award: Zero Emissions Noosa (ZEN) for Save Energy–Save Money (Business Energy Advisor)

In receiving her award Meghan Halverson said she had always believed in the spirit of collaborative care and working with others to do what’s best for the koalas, for the forests for the environment.

Among her work, which included the co-founding of Queensland Koala Crusaders Meghan said despite the destruction of habitat and the listing of koalas as endangered she remained hopeful because of the actions of those who refuse to accept destruction is inevitable, and in nature’s ability to heal.

NBRF Chair Fiona Berkin said the winners reflected the breadth of people caring for the region.

“Tonight’s winners show how people across the Noosa Biosphere are caring for the environment and for each other. We saw local businesses leading the way on sustainability, practical support to help businesses save energy, a program growing gardens and wellbeing together, and many individuals giving their time and energy to the place they love. Our awards received a record number of entries in 2026, reflecting a growing commitment to stewardship across the Noosa Biosphere”

NBRF Youth Representative Jarrah Small, and co-MC for the evening said the strong representation from young people was a highlight of the evening.

“It is inspiring to see more and more young people leading projects in their own backyard. The youth and school entries this year were thoughtful, hands-on, and driven by a genuine care for our biosphere. The next generation of custodians are here, and I’m so excited to see how all these projects and individuals continue to develop and grow”

NBRF thanked everyone who entered this year for sharing the work they do for our Noosa Biosphere. The judging panel, made up of Jordan Vance, Brian Keayes, Spencer Hitchen, Cr Tom Wegener, Rex Halverson, Linda Venables, and Hayley Holloway (Judging Moderator) had a tough job choosing between such a high standard of entries.

The Emerging Custodian Award winner received $500 towards their project, and the School or Class Biosphere Custodian Award winner received $2,000 towards their project. Both awards were sponsored by the Noosa Community Foundation.

Guests on the night heard of the contributions made by many people and organisations over many years to make Noosa the place it is today.

Co-MC for the evening Professor Ian Lowe told guests everyone nominated was a winner because they had all been recognised for the wonderful work they were doing to help this community and area that we love.

The night ended with a spectacular, surprise performance from Noosa Chorale who delighted the audience with their rendition of “What a Wonderful World”.

The 2026 Noosa Biosphere Awards were proudly supported by major event sponsor Noosa Council and presenting partner Unitywater. NBRF also thanks its category sponsors: the University of the Sunshine Coast, Noosa Community Foundation, Noosa 4 Sale, Bendigo Bank Tewantin-Noosa and Tourism Noosa.

Winners and finalists will be listed on the NBRF website at noosabiosphere.org.au/awards.

item.title: Share the Christmas spirit
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: Noosa Mayor Frank Wilkie is encouraging residents to help make Christmas brighter for local families and individuals facing hardship by […]
item.content:encoded:
Noosa Mayor Frank Wilkie is encouraging residents to help make Christmas brighter for local families and individuals facing hardship by supporting this year’s Mayor’s Christmas Appeal.

The annual appeal invites the community to donate gifts and gift cards for local charities to distribute to people doing it tough across Noosa this festive season.

Mayor Wilkie said while Christmas is a time for celebration, many people face financial pressures.

“Across our community, there are families feeling the strain of rising living costs and household expenses, and that pressure doesn’t disappear at Christmas,” Cr Wilkie said.

“The Mayor’s Christmas Appeal is a simple way for all of us to lend a hand and help bring some joy, comfort and hope to local people who might otherwise go without.”

Donations can be made from Monday, 16 November, to Monday, 14 December, and may include gift cards or new presents labelled with the suitable age and gender of the recipient .

Please note that perishables cannot be accepted.

This year’s appeal is supported by local charities St Vincent de Paul, Youturn, Santa’s Classy Helpers and Salvation Army Noosa, which will distribute donations to those in need.

Youturn General Manager, Community Services, Darce Foley, said that when members of the community are experiencing significant financial pressure, Christmas gifts are often one of the first things families and individuals go without.

“Supporting our Noosa Mayor’s Christmas Appeal is a meaningful way to help ensure that local people facing hardship can experience the warmth and spirit of Christmas, knowing that their community is standing alongside them,” he said.

Lorraine Kenway from Santa’s Classy Helpers said the appeal played an important role in helping local children experience the excitement of Christmas.

“Every year we meet families who are doing everything they can just to cover the basics,” Ms Kenway said.

“When someone donates a gift, they’re helping create special memories for children who might otherwise miss out on the magic of Christmas.”

Salvation Army Noosa’s Jacqueline Gluyas said community support was more important than ever.

“We see firsthand the challenges many families face, particularly at this time of year,” Ms Gluyas said.

“This appeal allows us to provide practical support while also giving people a sense of hope and connection during the festive season.”

Mayor Wilkie said gift cards were an excellent choice because they gave recipients the flexibility to buy what they needed most.

“Whether it’s a gift card or a thoughtfully chosen present, every donation helps make Christmas a little brighter for someone in our community,” Cr Wilkie sai

Donations can be dropped off between Monday 16 November and Monday 14 December at Noosa Council, 9 Pelican Street, Tewantin; Cooroy Library, 9 Maple Street, Cooroy or Tewantin-Noosa RSL Club, Memorial Avenue, Tewantin

Please attach a label to gifts showing the suitable age and gender of the intended recipient. For more information about the Mayor’s Christmas Appeal, visit noosa.qld.gov.au.

item.title: Pretty in Pink Encore
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: A second chance to own original art and help make a difference. The final bids may have been placed, but […]
item.content:encoded:
A second chance to own original art and help make a difference.

The final bids may have been placed, but the story of Studio One Noosa’s Pretty in Pink 2026 fundraiser is far from over.

Following another heartfelt year of creativity and generosity in support of the McGrath Foundation, Studio One Noosa is giving a beautiful collection of original artworks a second chance to find their forever homes.

Throughout November, the Encore Collection will be exhibited at The J, giving locals and visitors another opportunity to experience these beautiful works in person. The exhibition is open for viewing on weekdays and during evening events at the venue.

Each artwork has been generously donated by the participating artists, inspired by this year’s Terra Noosa theme, and represents an opportunity to bring something truly special into your home while supporting Cancer Care nurses through the McGrath Foundation.

With Christmas approaching, an original artwork could be the perfect gift, one that gives twice.

Every artwork deserves a home. Every sale makes a difference.

View and purchase the Encore Collection online at studioonenoosa.com.au

item.title: Visa changes welcomed
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: Noosa hotels, resorts and accommodation operators employing overseas workers in casual positions will have more time to prepare for changes […]
item.content:encoded:
Noosa hotels, resorts and accommodation operators employing overseas workers in casual positions will have more time to prepare for changes to Australia’s Working Holiday Maker visa program, with the Federal Government announcing a new system for second and third-year visas.

The changes have been welcomed by the Australian Hotels Association (AHA) and Accommodation Australia, which say the revised arrangements provide greater certainty for businesses and overseas workers heading into the busy summer tourism season.

Working Holiday Makers (WHMs) are an important part of the workforce across Noosa and the Sunshine Coast, filling casual positions in hotels, resorts, restaurants, cafes, sales and accommodation businesses.

For an industry heavily reliant on seasonal tourism and flexible staffing, the availability of overseas workers can be particularly important during peak holiday periods when demand for staff increases.

Under the changes announced by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke, existing Working Holiday Makers will have until February 28, 2027, to complete their specified regional work and lodge a valid application under the current arrangements.

From 1 March, 2027, people seeking a second or third Working Holiday Maker visa, excluding UK citizens, will need to hold a Next Year Regional Work Guarantee.

A registration portal will open on 1 December, with applicants registering their interest before being invited to apply.

The first monthly invitation round is expected in mid-January 2027, with registrations remaining valid until 30 June, 2027. Invitations will be valid for 12 months and allow recipients to apply for a visa.

The Government has allocated 45,000 second-year visa places and 25,000 third-year places in 2026-27.

The specified work requirement for a second visa will increase from three months to four months from March 1, where the requirement applies. Work completed before that date will count towards the new requirement.

The six-month specified work requirement for a third visa will remain unchanged.

The AHA and Accommodation Australia have described the changes as positive and pragmatic, following concerns raised by the tourism and hospitality industries about the proposed reforms.

AHA national chief executive Stephen Ferguson said the revised arrangements were a victory for common sense.

“This is a much better outcome for regional and remote Australia than when the new migration measures were first announced,” he said.

“All Australian businesses would prefer to hire Australians first, but where they can’t be found backpackers (WHM) fill the gaps and these changes are positive and pragmatic.”

Mr Ferguson said the industry would have preferred to retain the previous demand-driven system but acknowledged the Government had listened to its concerns.

“We can work with this new policy. Now we just need to get on with it and provide business and backpackers alike with some certainty,” he said.

Accommodation Australia chief executive James Goodwin also welcomed the changes, saying they recognised the contribution Working Holiday Makers made to the accommodation and tourism industry, particularly in regional areas.

“These are sensible and welcome changes which recognise the important contribution Working Holiday Makers make to Australia’s accommodation and tourism industry – particularly in the regions,” he said.

Mr Goodwin said delaying the start of the new arrangements would give businesses and workers more time to prepare ahead of the busy summer period.

He said the hotel industry would continue working with the Government to improve the processing of skilled visas, including for chefs, to ensure the industry had the right people in the right places.

Mr Burke said Working Holiday Makers made an important contribution to Australia’s economy, particularly in agriculture, tourism and hospitality and regional Australia.

“These changes give businesses and Working Holiday Makers clear rules and time to plan, while making sure the program continues to support the regions and industries that rely on it,” he said.

“Australia will continue to welcome Working Holiday Makers. These reforms make the program fairer, more targeted and sustainable for the long term.”

item.title: Claptos go bush
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: It’s not often The Claptomaniacs get the chance to play a Noosa hinterland venue up in them thar hills. “Being […]
item.content:encoded:
It’s not often The Claptomaniacs get the chance to play a Noosa hinterland venue up in them thar hills.

“Being a five-piece band kind of limits your choices, with some stages being built for soloists,” band drummer Alan Lander said.

“But I knew we had a couple of quiet weeks coming up and I wanted to take my bandmates up to play in my home town of Pomona.”

So, a quick word with Pomona Hotel owner Margaret L’Anson and a date was set up – this Sunday, November 22.

The Pomona Hotel has a fairly spacious stage area out back these days, with plenty of room for bigger bands.

“We’re looking forward to playing Pomona Hotel. We’ve only ever played the Majestic Theatre in Pomona, which is a fantastic experience,” Alan said.

“But Marg has done a great job developing the hotel as a valued entertainment venue.

“The Pomona Hotel also has a pretty extensive and value-for-money lunch menu these days, too, so it’s a very worthwhile destination for a Sunday afternoon.”

The Claptomaniacs will bring their repertoire of international hits from the late 60s to late 80s to the stage from 2pm, including material by Steely Dan, the Doobie Brothers, Joe Cocker, Boz Scaggs, Steve Miller Band, Robert Palmer and many more.

To book a table for lunch, call 5485 1187.

item.title: More than 200 charged
item.dc:creator: Jin Hui
item.description: A multi-disciplinary specialist team of Police within the Moreton District have hit a major milestone under Operation Yankee Tread, surpassing […]
item.content:encoded:
A multi-disciplinary specialist team of Police within the Moreton District have hit a major milestone under Operation Yankee Tread, surpassing 200 offenders charged.

Yankee Tread was launched in August to target dangerous driving behaviour across the district.

Since then, 244 people have been charged with 1156 offences and more 20 vehicles have been seized.

Around 3.15pm on 21 September, police received reports a silver Ford Falcon was committing burnouts on Bilby Drive, Maurice Avenue and Petersen Road in Morayfield.

Further enquiries led police to locate the vehicle outside a Morayfield address and it was subsequently impounded.

A 17-year-old Morayfield boy was charged with three counts of each dangerous operation of a motor vehicle, driving a motor vehicle without a licence SPER suspended, driving an uninsured vehicle, and driving an unregistered vehicle.

A second 17-year-old Morayfield boy was charged with three counts of unlawful conduct photographing a hooning group activity.

They are both next due to face Caboolture Childrens Court on 18 November.

Just after 10am on 7 October, a black Ford Falcon was observed being driven dangerously on Riccardo Street, Cottrill Road and Pumicestone Road in Caboolture.

Following subsequent investigations, police located the vehicle in Griffin where it was seized and impounded. An 18-year-old Kings Beach boy was also issued a Notice to Appear (NTA) for dangerous operation of a vehicle.

At approximately 8.20pm on 12 November, it is alleged police conducting patrols in Morayfield observed a grey Holden Commodore being driven dangerously on Morayfield Road while multiple people were hanging out of the vehicle.

The vehicle was intercepted a short time later near at Station Road. It will be alleged some the occupants attempted to run from police, before they were taken into custody.

A 17-year-old Naranga boy was charged with one count each of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle, obstructing police, face masked with intent to commit an indictable offence, driving over the general alcohol limit, driving as an unaccompanied learner, fail to display L plates, driving a defective vehicle, fail to attach number plates, and failing to transfer a vehicle.

He is due to face Caboolture Childrens Court on 18 November.

An 18-year-old Redcliffe man was also charged with obstruct police and is due to face Caboolture Magistrates Court on 24 November.

Moreton Assistant District Officer Superintendent Chris Toohey said there has been a significant reduction in hooning complaints since the launch of Yankee Tread.

“Police have seen a 34% decrease in weekend hooning complaints which is traditionally the period of highest demand for these offences,” he said.

“Overall, hooning complaints are down 29% in Clontarf, 26% in Narangba, 20% in Deception Bay, 16% in Caboolture and nearly 11% in Morayfield.”

Superintendent Toohey said while these results are promising, officers will not become complacent.

“Moreton Police are committed to continuing to disrupt offender behaviour to improve road safety outcomes across the district.”

Queensland residents are encouraged to report dangerous driving behaviour directly to 13HOON (134 666) or Policelink (131 444). The information you provide is relayed to police for further investigation and allows officers to locate hotspots and take action to prevent it reoccurring.

You can also report online, where you can upload photos and videos: www.police.qld.gov.au/policelink-reporting/hooning-launch

If it is happening now or it is a life-threatening situation, please call Triple Zero (000).
